H&M Group, founded in 1947 in Sweden, is a global fashion retailer with over 4,000 stores in 79 markets. It offers a wide range of apparel and accessories under various brands, committed to sustainability and affordable fashion.

## History

History section provides information on new products, mergers, acquisitions, expansions, approvals, and many more key events. [...] H & M Hennes & Mauritz AB (H&M), a subsidiary of Ramsbury Invest AB, is a retailer of fashion apparel and accessories. The company’s product portfolio includes t-shirts, sweatshirts, shirts, sports and swimwear, shorts, cardigans, sweaters, blazer suits, and lingerie. It also offers accessories such as jewelry, hats and gloves, belts and suspenders, home textiles, homeware, sunglasses, and watches. The company markets its products under the H&M, H&M Home, H&M Move, H&M Beauty, ARKET, AFound, [...] ARKET, AFound, Monki, COS, Cheap Monday, Weekday, Sellpy, & Other Stories, and Singular Society brand names. H&M sells its products through both brick-and-mortar stores and various e-commerce channels. The company’s operations are spread across Europe, Africa, the Americas, Asia, and Oceania. H&M is headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden.

H&M is among the largest fashion retailers worldwide. The company is committed to providing in a sustainable manner the best offerings and experience to customers so that they can dress according to their personal style. Erling Persson opened the first store in 1947 in Västerås, Sweden. The store was originally called Hennes (“hers” in Swedish) and only offered women's wear. In 1968 the company acquired Mauritz Widforss, a hunting apparel company, which led to the store offering men’s apparel [...] men’s apparel and the change of the name to Hennes & Mauritz. H&M collaborates with high-end designers and runs marketing campaigns with celebrities.

Back to top

# Our history

Our founder had a vision. Erling Persson wanted to make great fashion available and affordable to everyone and do this in the right way. From a single store in 1947 we became a family of brands offering fashion and design to customers worldwide. This is our story.

## The ’40s and ’50s

#### 1947 [...] During these decades, the international growth begins. Norway comes first, followed by Denmark, the UK, and Switzerland.

The growth pace increases even further, with five or six new stores opening every year.

#### 1973

 – Hennes & Mauritz starts selling underwear.
 – ABBA-member Anni-Frid Lyngstad becomes the first “supermodel” to be photographed for the company.

#### 1974 [...] #### 1974

 – Hennes & Mauritz is listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange.
 – The stores are rebranded with the abbreviation “H&M”.

#### 1977

 – Teenagers get their own version of H&M as the Impuls concept is launched, inspired by denim stores in the US.
 – H&M introduces cosmetics into its assortment.

## The ’80s and ’90s

In the 1980s, the foundation is laid for the upcoming global expansion. New openings include the first H&M stores in Germany and the Netherlands.

H&M's primary revenue comes from retail sales, supplemented by franchising, licensing, and wholesale distribution. It also earns income from subsidiary brands and partnerships. The company invests in circular business models and second-hand fashion.

## Revenue Streams

Retail sales of clothing and accessories through stores and online channels generate the largest share of H&M's revenue. Franchising and licensing fees contribute income from markets where local partners operate under the H&M brand. Wholesale distribution to other retailers, designer collaborations and limited editions and revenue from subsidiary brands including COS, Monki and Weekday round out the company's income sources. [...] H&M built one of the world's largest fashion retailers by combining fast fashion design cycles with affordable pricing, wide store networks and a growing online presence. Founded in 1947 in Västerås, Sweden, by Erling Persson, the company expanded from a single women's clothing shop into a group spanning thousands of stores across dozens of markets, plus subsidiary brands including COS, Monki and Weekday. Its revenue comes primarily from in-store and online retail sales, supplemented by [...] H&M's business model depends on translating runway trends into affordable clothing quickly enough to keep customers returning to stores and its website. Retail sales through company-operated stores and online channels generate the majority of revenue, while franchising, wholesale distribution and limited-edition designer collaborations add supplementary income. The company has faced growing scrutiny over the environmental impact of fast fashion, prompting investment in recycling programs and

New growth and ventures. We are creating new revenue streams through a variety of strategic partnerships and new circular business models, and we see great potential in the companies that we invest in. One example is Sellpy, which is growing rapidly in 24 European markets as demand for second-hand fashion continues to increase. Our investments in innovation also mean we are taking important steps on our journey towards circularity. Through greater use of recycled and more sustainably produced
